tick_semantics: one row per completed driver service, named in each row's service field. Two kinds qualify: the one-shot DriverInit that precedes the first vertical interrupt (kind 6, completing where the first zVInt begins), and every zVInt return (kind 3). 5400 movie frames yield 5263 ticks: pre-install frames run no service, and a frame whose driver work overruns it contributes no row because zVInt reaches its return in the following frame. Movie frame 252, the title-music load, is such a frame; its service completes in frame 253.
sampling: driver RAM 1C00h..1FA0h captured by the observer core as a completion snapshot on the driver's own service boundaries: the zVInt ret at Z80 PC 0084h (skdisasm Sound/Z80 Sound Driver.asm:520; the ;loc_85 comment at :522 pins the address) and the DriverInit completion at PC 0038h. Never mid-invocation.
writes_partition: ordered YM/PSG writes partitioned by the same service-completion boundary, so every write appears exactly once in stream order. residual_write_count are the writes after the final completed service, which belong to no tick.

supersedes.reason: v1 declared sampling post_invocation but read the RAM out of band after the frame advanced, so music-load frames recorded a truncated prefix of zUpdateMusic's track-iteration order. That is what stalled the oracle at v1 tick 138, movie frame 252.
supersedes.status: retired; retained unmodified for provenance and not compared

content: boot, SEGA chant, title music (mus 25h), file select, Knuckles intro theme (mus 1Fh), AIZ1 music (mus 01h) with gameplay SFX
duplicate_capture: two serial captures to separate external roots were byte-identical at sha256 c8174a3f150409bb2511c09b85d511ffd6acd98aff8abc682c1f52f632623f06
boot_boundary: the DriverInit row carries 84 Z80 writes, ending at ym port 0 register 27h. v1's frame-granular projection reported 85 for its boot service because it swept the whole frame, taking in the 2Bh write that the first vertical interrupt actually owns.

frame_shape.zero_service_pre_install_range: movie frames 0-13, before the 68k has loaded the driver
frame_shape.note: A zero-service frame is one the driver's work ran past, so the Z80 misses that frame's vertical interrupt and zVInt reaches its return in a later frame. Movie frame 252, the title-music load, is one. The longest contiguous block begins at frame 64 and is zPlaySEGAPCM, which disables interrupts for its whole transport. double_service_frames is 0 across this window: 0084h is reached once per interrupt, and the movie is NTSC so the PAL double-update path never runs.

request_sidecar.production_bound_meaning: The sidecar's own metadata carries production_bound:false and that value is preserved verbatim; the reader refuses any sidecar that claims otherwise. Publication installs a reviewed capture as a committed comparison-side driver input. It does not bind the observation to a production producer, and it gives the sidecar no authority over any compared value: the sidecar supplies only the mailbox byte a service consumes, exactly as the S1 tool supplies the song it plays. Every compared value still comes from the engine alone.
request_sidecar.what_it_supplies: The 68k-written zMusicNumber byte for the movie rows this stream's frame-entry mailbox sampling cannot show. mailbox_sampling is frame_entry, so a request written and consumed before the next sampled frame entry is invisible; movie row 242's cmd_StopSEGA (0FEh) is such a request and is what stalled the v2 oracle at tick 128.
request_sidecar.observation_site: Z80 RAM 1C0Ah read at 68k PC 01370h, the move.w #0,$A11100 bus release that follows the request store, while the Z80 was still stopped. Recorded as observed_at_pc/observed_opcode/mailbox_address in the sidecar itself.
request_sidecar.window: movie rows [0,5400), the same power-on window as the reference

request_sidecar.capture_paths_note: Two distinct absent external paths under a session scratch root, outside the repository; recorded for provenance, not as a re-runnable location.

observer.note: The same observer core family as the v2 reference; the request action reads the mailbox at the 68k store site and emits no compared value.

request_sidecar.resolution: A sidecar row R is resolved against service ticks by the reader, never by a frame index in the fixture. See S3kAudioReferenceReader.resolveSidecarRequests for the rule and its derivation from this stream's own frame-entry samples.
request_sidecar.notes: Human approval for publication was granted on 2026-09-03 as part of the roadmap, after the duplicate-capture gate was met. The oracle defaults to this file; S3kAudioParityTool's --requests option remains an override.
